I will keep the farm split between the system I know best and the crop that gives me some income diversification. I will put 25 mu into the wheat-maize rotation and keep 10 mu in cotton. I have 45 years of experience, I can irrigate from wells, and I have a small household, so I will stay with a plan that is stable, familiar, and manageable rather than chasing anything complicated. On the wheat land, I will use improved wheat seed, keep fertility fairly strong, irrigate enough to protect the key growth stages, and aim for a solid, reliable yield. After wheat harvest, I will no-till seed hybrid maize on the same 25 mu so I can save time, conserve moisture, and make full use of the season. On the cotton land, I will use hybrid seed, give more potassium and more crop protection than grain crops, and irrigate several times because cotton responds well when water is steady. I will keep inputs at a level that matches an irrigated farm in my area: not too low to limit yield, not too high to waste money.
